_comment: Recovered by recover_source_map.mjs — bucket objects are byte-identical to Processed_small/<variant>/<source-name>.webp, which carries the source clip name. Regenerate with that script; do not hand-edit.

female/single-arm-band-chest-press.note: Needs to be a single arm

female/barbell-floor-press.note: Needs to be on the floor and not on a bench

female/barbell-guillotine-press.note: Standard bench press shown — bar to mid-chest. The guillotine lowers the bar to the THROAT, wide grip, elbows flared level with the shoulders.

female/barbell-jm-press.note: Standard bench press shown. The JM press is a close-grip bench / skullcrusher hybrid: hands 15-18in apart, bar lowered toward the throat with the elbows staying FORWARD of the bar, then pressed straight up rather than in an arc.

female/barbell-larsen-press.note: Standard bench press shown, feet planted. The Larsen press is done with the LEGS STRAIGHT OUT AND FEET OFF THE FLOOR — no leg drive. That is the whole exercise.

female/barbell-box-squat.note: needs to be a box and not a bench

female/barbell-yates-row.note: Bent-over row shown - torso parallel to the floor, overhand grip. The Yates row is more upright (about 45 degrees) with an UNDERHAND grip, pulling to the lower abdomen.

female/barbell-hang-clean.note: The clip is a clean-grip FRONT SQUAT — a different lift. The hang clean starts standing with the bar already held at mid-thigh, then pulls it explosively to the front rack. No pull from the floor, no squat down from the rack.

female/axle-deadlift.note: Standard barbell shown. An axle is a thick 2-inch smooth bar, which changes the grip completely and usually the load with it.

female/barbell-deficit-deadlift.note: Standard deadlift from the floor shown. The deficit version has the lifter STANDING ON A 1-2 INCH PLATFORM or plate, so the bar starts lower relative to the feet and the pull is longer.

female/barbell-walking-lunge.note: Stationary barbell lunge - the athlete returns to the start each rep. A walking lunge steps through and advances.

female/ez-bar-overhead-triceps-extension.note: Needs to be an EZ bar

female/battle-rope-circles.note: Clip shows alternating up-and-down waves. Circles rotate each arm in a circular path so the ropes trace loops.

female/battle-rope-double-waves.note: Clip shows ALTERNATING waves - the ropes are out of phase. Double waves drive both ropes up and down together, in phase.

female/battle-rope-lateral-waves.note: Clip shows alternating VERTICAL waves. Lateral waves sweep the ropes side to side, out and in.

female/battle-rope-slams.note: Clip shows continuous alternating waves. A slam raises both rope ends overhead and drives them into the floor as one explosive rep.

female/cable-decline-chest-press.note: Decline and cable correct, but it needs to be a chest press and not a fly

female/cable-belt-squat.note: Cable goblet squat - the handle is held at the chest, not hung from the hips.

female/cable-front-squat.note: Cable goblet squat - the handle is held at the chest in both hands. A front squat racks the load across the shoulders.

female/cable-incline-chest-press.note: Needs to be incline cable chest press and not fly

female/bayesian-cable-curl.note: One-arm cable curl shown. A Bayesian curl turns the back to a LOW pulley and lets the cable draw the arm behind the torso, starting the biceps fully stretched.

female/behind-the-back-cable-lateral-rai.note: One-arm cable lateral raise with the cable running in front of the body. The behind-the-back version routes the cable behind, which loads the bottom of the range.

female/dumbbell-push-press.note: Needs to be both at the same time

female/cable-bulgarian-split-squat.note: Dumbbell Bulgarian split squat - correct movement, wrong implement. The cable version holds a handle from a low pulley.

female/double-kettlebell-clean.note: Right motion, needs to be kettlebells

female/band-goblet-squat.note: Needs a band and not a dumbbell

female/dumbbell-seal-row.note: Incline row shown - torso angled, feet driving into the floor. A seal row lies fully prone on a FLAT bench with the arms hanging straight down and no leg contact at all.

female/cable-y-raise.note: Dumbbell incline Y-raise - the Y shape is right, the implement and the bench are not. A cable Y-raise is done standing at two low pulleys.

female/barbell-thruster.note: Dumbbell thruster shown. The barbell version racks the bar across the front of the shoulders; the movement - front squat straight into an overhead press - is otherwise identical.

female/double-kettlebell-press.note: Right motion, but the kettlebells need to go up at the same time

female/kettlebell-push-press.note: Needs to be both moving at the same time

female/converging-chest-press.note: Standard lever chest press shown, handles travelling straight forward. A converging press arcs the handles inward toward each other at lockout.

female/reverse-pec-deck.note: Needs to be reversed. Same machine

female/cycling-intervals.note: Steady pedalling on an upright stationary bike. Intervals are a pacing prescription a looping clip cannot show.

female/suspension-trainer-atomic-push-up.note: Plain suspension push-up shown. The atomic version adds a knee tuck to the chest at the top of every rep.

female/suspension-trainer-high-row.note: Mid-height row shown. A high row pulls toward the face with the elbows flared wide, working the rear delts rather than the mid-back.

female/suspension-trainer-low-row.note: Mid-height row shown. A low row keeps the elbows tight to the ribs and pulls toward the waist.

female/band-reverse-lunge.note: Bodyweight reverse lunge shown — there is no band. Needs a resistance band under the front foot, held at shoulder height.

female/burpee-box-jump.note: It's showing the burpee but not the box jump

female/box-jump-over.note: Plain box jump - the athlete jumps up and comes back down the same side. A box jump OVER continues across and lands on the far side, then repeats back.

female/bodyweight-good-morning.note: Correct bodyweight good morning - hands behind the head, hinge at the hips - but performed with a WIDE stance. The standard version is hip-width.

male/single-arm-cable-overhead-triceps-e.note: Needs to be a cable machine

male/single-arm-band-chest-press.note: Needs to be a chest press not a fly

male/box-squat-to-bench.note: Barbell bench squat shown. This exercise is BODYWEIGHT, so there should be no bar on the back - the squat-to-bench motion itself is correct.

male/barbell-push-jerk.note: The clip is a full CLEAN AND JERK — it pulls the bar off the floor first. The push jerk starts with the bar already in the front rack: dip, drive with the legs, press under the bar and catch it with locked elbows in a partial squat.

male/barbell-yates-row.note: Pendlay row shown - torso parallel to the floor, overhand grip. The Yates row is far more upright (about 45 degrees) and uses an UNDERHAND grip, pulling to the lower abdomen.

male/battle-rope-circles.note: Clip shows alternating up-and-down waves. Circles rotate each arm in a circular path so the ropes trace loops.

male/battle-rope-double-waves.note: Clip shows ALTERNATING waves - the ropes are out of phase. Double waves drive both ropes up and down together, in phase.

male/battle-rope-lateral-waves.note: Clip shows alternating VERTICAL waves. Lateral waves sweep the ropes side to side, out and in.

male/bayesian-cable-curl.note: Drag curl shown, facing the stack. A Bayesian curl faces AWAY from a low pulley with the arm drawn behind the torso, so the biceps starts fully stretched.

male/behind-the-back-cable-lateral-raise.note: One-arm cable lateral raise with the cable running in front of the body. The behind-the-back version routes the cable behind, which loads the bottom of the range.

male/close-grip-cable-seated-row.note: Seated cable row with a supine (underhand) close grip. A close-grip seated row normally uses a neutral V-bar with the palms facing each other.

male/cable-belt-squat.note: Cable squat shown - the cable runs between the legs from a low pulley rather than from a belt around the hips. The loading position is effectively the same.

male/active-hang.note: Dead hang shown - shoulders fully relaxed and up by the ears. An active hang holds the scapulae pulled DOWN and back, which is the entire point of the exercise.

male/dumbbell-chest-supported-row.note: Needs to be a row but good chest support

male/band-goblet-squat.note: Needs be a band not a dumbbell

male/incline-dumbbell-rear-delt-fly.note: Bent-over rear fly shown. The incline version lies chest-down on an inclined bench, which takes the lower back out of the movement.

male/converging-chest-press.note: Standard lever chest press shown, handles travelling straight forward. A converging press arcs the handles inward toward each other at lockout.

male/reverse-pec-deck.note: Needs to be reversed. Same machine

male/chest-to-bar-pull-up.note: Standard pull-up - the chin clears the bar. A chest-to-bar pull-up is pulled higher, until the chest touches the bar.

male/smith-machine-romanian-deadlift.note: Full deadlift from the floor shown. A Romanian deadlift starts at the top, keeps the knees nearly locked and lowers only to mid-shin without resetting on the floor.

male/cycling-intervals.note: Steady pedalling on an upright stationary bike. Intervals are a pacing prescription - alternating hard and easy - which a looping clip cannot show.

male/depth-drop.note: Just need the drop not the jump

male/cable-bulgarian-split-squat.note: Bodyweight Bulgarian split squat - rear foot elevated, correct movement, no cable. The cable version holds a handle from a low pulley.

male/cable-dead-bug.note: Bodyweight dead bug shown. The cable version holds a handle overhead with the arms straight throughout, so the lats stay loaded while the limbs move.

male/band-shoulder-external-rotation.note: No band in the clip — the arm rotates unloaded. Needs a band anchored at the side, elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked to the ribs, forearm rotating OUTWARD away from the body.

male/band-shoulder-internal-rotation.note: No band in the clip — the arm rotates unloaded. Needs a band anchored at the side, elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked to the ribs, forearm rotating INWARD across the body.

male/single-leg-sit-to-stand.note: Needs to be sit to stand

male/box-step-off-landing.note: Step UP onto the box shown - this drill steps DOWN off the box and absorbs the landing in a soft athletic position. The clip runs the movement in the opposite direction.

male/barbell-overhead-carry.note: Wrong implement — the clip is a KETTLEBELL overhead carry. Needs a barbell held overhead in two hands, walking.

male/cable-sled-drag.note: Weighted power sled shown. The cable version runs off a cable stack with a rope or belt, so the resistance is a constant pull rather than ground friction.
